case_name: Jasdeep Kaur vs Amit Dhillon And Anr
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Marriage of the petitioner with the respondent was solemnized on 28.03.2016. Due to matrimonial discord the parties are living separately since March, 2023. The petitioner has no source of income and is fully dependent upon her parents.

legal_principles.principle: The ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
legal_principles.held: In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. SaravanaKarthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial matters, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties.
legal_principles.held: The Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. SaravanaKarthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: The wife's convenience should be looked at while considering transfer.
legal_principles.held: Given the prevailing socioeconomic paradigm in the Indian society, generally, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at while considering transfer.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. SaravanaKarthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: When two or more proceedings are pending in different Courts between the same parties which raise common question of fact and law, they should be tried together by the same Judge.
legal_principles.held: It is desirable that they should be tried together by the same Judge so as to avoid multiplicity in trial of the same issues and conflict of decisions.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. SaravanaKarthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

outcome.final_order: Reply on behalf of contesting respondent No. 1 filed along with the application is taken on record.
